title: Room at the front of the line
hook: Six items fill a row of slots. One more must go first. What does it cost?

doesNotKnow: that a row of slots (an array) must shift everything to insert at the front
that a chain (a linked list) is cheap to insert into but slow to walk

misconception: Inserting is equally cheap in any structure.
objective: The learner can explain that inserting at the front of a 6-item array moves all 6 items, while a linked list moves none but needs 3 hops to reach item 4.

claims.text: Inserting a new item at the front of a row of 6 items in numbered slots moves all 6 existing items one slot right.
claims.source: Each item i must go from slot i to slot i + 1 to free slot 1: n = 6 moves (CLRS, Introduction to Algorithms, 3rd ed., ch. 10 intro: arrays store elements contiguously). Demo.tsx ROW_MOVES = ITEMS.length.

claims.text: Inserting at the front of a chain moves no items: the new box's arrow and the start arrow are set, 2 arrows in all.
claims.source: LIST-INSERT in CLRS 3rd ed., 10.2 (singly linked case: x.next = L.head; L.head = x). Demo.tsx CHAIN_MOVES = 0, CHAIN_ARROWS = 2.

claims.text: Reaching item 4 of a chain takes 3 hops along the arrows; in general item k takes k − 1 hops.
claims.source: Starting at the first box, each hop follows one next-arrow, so item k is k − 1 hops away (CLRS 10.2, LIST-SEARCH walks from the head). Demo.tsx HOPS = TARGET − 1.

claims.text: In a row of numbered slots, any slot is reached in a single jump.
claims.source: Array indexing computes the address from the index in constant time (CLRS 3rd ed., 10.3 and Appendix on memory as an array of words).

claims.text: A row of slots is called an array and a chain of boxes joined by arrows is called a linked list.

recall.question: You keep a list where you constantly add items at the front and rarely look up the 500th item. Which structure suits it?
recall.why: A chain inserts at the front by setting two arrows; a row would shift every item each time. The chain's slow walk barely matters if lookups are rare.
